title: edges: Implement EDG-* core binding tests
description: Implement regression tests for edge binding reliability to ensure node connections persist during movement and transforms.

ubiquitous: THE SYSTEM SHALL maintain DAG integrity for all edge operations

event_driven.trigger: WHEN a bound node is moved
event_driven.shall: THE SYSTEM SHALL recalculate and update connected edge endpoints

unwanted.condition: IF a node movement causes an invalid state
unwanted.shall_not: THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT break existing valid edge bindings
unwanted.because: edges must remain securely attached to their source and target nodes

preconditions: Nodes involved in edge binding must exist
postconditions: Edge endpoints match the boundaries of connected nodes

happy: Moving a single node updates all connected edges correctly
Moving a group of connected nodes preserves all relative edge bindings
error: Attempting to bind an edge to a non-existent node fails gracefully
Creating a binding that results in a circular dependency is rejected

questions: How are edge endpoints currently recalculated?

title: edges: Fix edge binding regressions discovered by EDG tests
description: Resolve any failing tests from the EDG test suite to ensure edge bindings are 100% reliable during node transforms.

ubiquitous: THE SYSTEM SHALL reliably anchor edges to node perimeters during any transform

event_driven.trigger: WHEN multiple bound nodes are resized
event_driven.shall: THE SYSTEM SHALL proportionally adjust all internal edge connections

unwanted.condition: IF an edge is disconnected due to a deletion
unwanted.shall_not: THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT leave dangling edge references in the state
unwanted.because: every edge must have a valid source and target

postconditions: All EDG-* tests pass without regressions
invariants: Every EdgeId corresponds to an edge with valid source and target NodeIds

happy: Edges successfully remain attached during complex grouped resizing operations
Reconnecting an edge correctly updates the target node and triggers re-render
error: Edge reconnections that violate DAG constraints revert to previous state
Dangling edges from invalid state imports are pruned gracefully

questions: Why are edges detaching during multi-select operations?

phase_0: Run EDG test suite and categorize failures
phase_1: Fix multi-select transform edge detachment bugs

title: viewport: Implement multi-diagram view data structures
description: Add support for managing multiple diagram documents in memory simultaneously.

ubiquitous: THE SYSTEM SHALL support storing multiple active diagram documents in memory

event_driven.trigger: WHEN a user opens a second diagram
event_driven.shall: THE SYSTEM SHALL load it into an isolated state container without overwriting the first

unwanted.condition: IF memory limits are approached with multiple open diagrams
unwanted.because: it must gracefully degrade or prevent opening more documents

preconditions: At least one document is open
postconditions: New document is registered in the active workspace manager
invariants: Each diagram maintains its own independent undo/redo history stack

happy: User can open three distinct diagrams and switch between them
Each diagram maintains its separate dirty state
error: Attempting to load a corrupted diagram doesn't affect other open diagrams
Exceeding open diagram limit shows a user-friendly error message

questions: How to structure the root state to hold multiple documents?

phase_0: Design Workspace struct to hold multiple documents
phase_2: Update UI state to reflect active document

title: ui: Implement tabbed interface for multi-diagram view
description: Build a Dioxus tabbed UI to switch between multiple open diagrams.

ubiquitous: THE SYSTEM SHALL render a tab bar showing all open diagrams

event_driven.trigger: WHEN a user clicks a diagram tab
event_driven.shall: THE SYSTEM SHALL make the selected diagram active and render it

unwanted.condition: IF a user attempts to close a diagram with unsaved changes
unwanted.shall_not: THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT close it immediately
unwanted.because: the user must confirm they want to discard unsaved changes

preconditions: Workspace state contains list of open documents
postconditions: Active document is updated in UI state upon tab click
invariants: The tab bar accurately reflects the titles and dirty states of all open documents

happy: Clicking a background tab brings that document's canvas to the front
Closing a clean document tab removes it without prompting
error: Closing a dirty document triggers a discard confirmation dialog
Failing to save a document during the close prompt keeps the tab open

questions: How to manage tab state and rendering efficiently in Dioxus?

phase_1: Wire up tab clicks to workspace state active document
phase_2: Implement close confirmation dialog for dirty tabs

title: build: Establish desktop and web CI build verification
description: Add CI pipelines to ensure the codebase compiles successfully for both desktop and wasm32 targets.

ubiquitous: THE SYSTEM SHALL compile for both desktop and web targets without platform-specific regressions

event_driven.trigger: WHEN code is pushed to the main branch
event_driven.shall: THE SYSTEM SHALL run both desktop and wasm builds in CI

unwanted.condition: IF a platform-specific dependency breaks the web build
unwanted.shall_not: THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT allow the PR to be merged
unwanted.because: the web and desktop targets must remain in sync

preconditions: Rust toolchain with wasm32-unknown-unknown target is installed
postconditions: CI reports separate pass/fail statuses for desktop and web builds
invariants: Core logic contains no incompatible platform-specific code

happy: A clean commit builds successfully on both desktop and wasm32
CI correctly reports a green status when both builds succeed
error: Adding a tokio dependency fails the wasm32 build and halts the CI pipeline
A desktop-only native file system API call fails the web build

questions: What is the current CI setup for Dioxus web vs desktop?

phase_1: Add desktop build step to CI workflow

title: tests: Conduct cross-platform performance baseline testing
description: Measure and document 3000-node performance metrics across both Desktop and Web platforms.

ubiquitous: THE SYSTEM SHALL maintain performance metrics logs for both desktop and web builds

event_driven.trigger: WHEN the performance test suite is executed
event_driven.shall: THE SYSTEM SHALL output FPS and memory usage for both platforms

unwanted.condition: IF the web build runs significantly slower than desktop
unwanted.shall_not: THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT silently ignore the discrepancy
unwanted.because: performance parity is a key requirement for the unified codebase

postconditions: Performance numbers are recorded in a benchmark log
invariants: Measurements are taken under standardized load conditions

happy: Desktop app maintains 120 FPS during a pan operation with 3000 nodes
Web app maintains at least 60 FPS during identical pan operations
error: If memory limit exceeds 500MB, the test fails explicitly
If frames drop below 30 FPS, the test records a critical failure

questions: How can we accurately measure WebAssembly rendering FPS?
